name: What Should I Do if Cabinets Arrive With Incorrect Measurements?

mainEntity.name: Who pays if kitchen cabinets do not fit because the renovation measurements were wrong?
mainEntity.text: Who pays if kitchen cabinets do not fit because the renovation measurements were wrong?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cabinet dimensions should be verified after walls, floors, appliances, and plumbing conditions are confirmed. The contract should state who performs the final field measure, who approves shop drawings, and who is responsible for errors caused by inaccurate measurements or unreported site conditions. If cabinets do not fit, photograph every mismatch, preserve packaging and labels, and compare the delivered pieces with the approved drawings. Do not allow workers to hide a major error with excessive fillers, uneven gaps, altered doors, or improvised panels unless the revised solution is professionally drawn and approved. Stop work that could make replacement more difficult. Request a written explanation identifying the error, replacement parts, temporary protection, revised installation date, and any added cost. Ask who pays for rework, storage, labor, countertop changes, appliance delays, and related finishing. A reliable process includes a pre-fabrication field measure, appliance specifications, corner dimensions, filler plans, and signed shop drawings. The lowest bid is risky if it lacks these controls.
acceptedAnswer.description: Responsibility depends on the contract, measurement process, approved drawings, and cause of the error. Before fabrication, require field verification and written approval of cabinet dimensions. If cabinets arrive incorrectly sized, document the mismatch immediately, stop irreversible installation, notify the responsible parties in writing, and request a correction plan with costs and schedule impacts.
